question: Fill in the blank: The Defence of India Act, 1915 empowered authorities to ____.
solution:
The correct answer is __**enforce detention**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Defence of India Act, 1915 was enacted during World War I by the British government to address security concerns and ensure control over revolutionary activities.
 
• The Act empowered authorities to enforce detention without trial, aiming to suppress dissent and revolutionary movements in India.
 
• Its provisions granted extensive powers to the government to curb activities deemed as threats to public safety or national security.
 
• The Act was implemented to counter revolutionary activities, especially those linked to the Ghadar Party and other groups opposing British rule.
 
• It included measures such as preventive detention, censorship of the press, and restrictions on free speech and assembly.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Mandate recruitment (Option 2):**

 
 
• The Defence of India Act, 1915 did not directly mandate recruitment for military services; its focus was primarily on maintaining internal security.
 
• Recruitment during World War I was carried out through separate policies and mechanisms established by the colonial government.
 
• Indian soldiers were extensively recruited to serve in World War I, but this was not linked to the Defence of India Act.
 
 
 
• **Form councils (Option 3):**
 
 
• The Act did not have provisions for forming councils or administrative bodies.
 
• Council formations in colonial India were typically addressed through other legislative measures, such as the Government of India Acts.
 
• The Defence of India Act was solely aimed at suppressing revolutionary activities and securing the British regime during wartime.
 
 
 
• **Restrict arms imports (Option 4):**
 
 
• While the Defence of India Act, 1915 dealt with security measures, it did not specifically focus on restricting arms imports.
 
• The regulation of arms imports was governed by other acts and policies, such as the Arms Act of 1878.
 
• However, the Act may have indirectly impacted arms imports by empowering authorities to take preventive actions against potential threats.
 
 
 
• **Purpose of the Defence of India Act:**
 
 
• The Act marked the colonial government’s attempt to strengthen its control during wartime.
 
• Its provisions were criticized for being repressive and infringing on civil liberties.
 
• The Act served as a precursor to similar wartime legislation enacted during World War II, including the Defence of India Rules, 1939.
